about_page_description: I build the systems that make sound work.
about_journey_p1: I have a background in classical piano, but I never felt at home just performing. I needed to know *how* the sound worked. That curiosity pushed me from music school into physics and math, and eventually to Game Audio. Now, I don't just design sounds; I write the C++ and Python tools to make them run effectively in real-time.
about_journey_p2: I've built an ML system that recognizes beatbox patterns in real-time because standard tools were too slow. I've written custom Wwise fixers because I got tired of manual repairs after Perforce merges. I'm currently at DAE in Belgium, learning how to channel this obsession into professional game development.
about_drives_p1: It's about solving the puzzle. Why are footsteps triggering on the wrong surface? Why is the memory budget blown? In *Not Today Darling*, I optimized audio assets specifically for 4-player shared-screen performance because we didn't have room for waste.
about_drives_p2: I also love building tools. When Wwise kept breaking after Perforce pulls on *Shadow Frames*, I didn't just complain; I wrote a script to fix it automatically. Small efficiency gains add up to shipped games.
contact_subtitle: I usually reply within 1-2 days. Available for game audio, tool development, and middleware integration.

principle_layering_desc: I design sounds in layers: transient for punch, body for weight, texture for character. Parameters (speed, intensity, distance) blend them in real-time. Sounds respond to gameplay.

dataasset.label: DataAsset Pattern
dataasset.desc: Pure data container - no logic, just editor-exposed properties. Designers create instances, assign Wwise events and tweak values. No C++ recompilation needed.

wwise.label: Wwise Reference
wwise.desc: TObjectPtr to Wwise asset. Audio events, RTPCs, switches - all assigned in editor. Zero hardcoded strings. Change audio by swapping asset references.

hysteresis.label: Hysteresis Values
hysteresis.desc: Start/Stop thresholds prevent audio flickering. Designers tune these per-enemy without code changes. Meta tags add editor validation.

reflection.label: Runtime Reflection
reflection.desc: GetClass() returns actual runtime type. For BP_GhostAnomaly inheriting from ABaseAnomaly, this returns BP_GhostAnomaly class.

hierarchy.label: Inheritance Walk
hierarchy.desc: Walks up class hierarchy until settings found. BP_GhostAnomaly → AGhostAnomaly → ABaseAnomaly. First match wins - most specific takes priority.

tmap.label: TMap Lookup
tmap.desc: TMap<TSubclassOf<ABaseAnomaly>, FAnomalyAudioSettings> - designers map anomaly classes to audio switches in editor. Add new anomaly = add row in DataAsset.

struct.label: DataTable Row
struct.desc: FTableRowBase enables DataTable integration. Each row = one dialogue entry with Wwise switch + duration. CSV import/export friendly.

datatable.label: Audio Metadata
datatable.desc: DataTable holds audio config - which Wwise switch, how long to display subtitle. Separate from actual text for cleaner localization.

stringtable.label: Localized Text
stringtable.desc: StringTable for dialogue text - Unreal's native localization system. Same AnomalyID key in both tables. Text team edits StringTable, audio team edits DataTable.

proximity.label: Proximity Callback
proximity.desc: This function is called by EnemyPresenceComponent whenever the distance to the nearest enemy changes. ProximityValue is normalized 0-100%.

hysteresis.label: Hysteresis Thresholds
hysteresis.desc: Two separate thresholds prevent audio flickering. StartThreshold (e.g. 20%) triggers audio ON, StopThreshold (e.g. 10%) triggers OFF. This gap prevents rapid toggling.

dread.label: Dread Layers
dread.desc: Posts a Wwise Event that starts layered ambient dread sounds - low drones, unsettling textures. These layers intensify based on RTPC value.

breathing.label: Stress Breathing
breathing.desc: Triggers stressed breathing loop. Plays on top of dread layers when enemy is close.

rtpc.label: RTPC Update
rtpc.desc: Real-Time Parameter Control - sends ProximityValue to Wwise. Controls volume, filter cutoff, and pitch in real-time. Smooth transitions, no hard cuts.

intensity.label: Breathing Intensity
intensity.desc: Separate RTPC for breathing rate. Scales with enemy proximity.

surface.label: Surface Detection
surface.desc: Returns an FName that maps directly to a Wwise Switch value. FootstepAudioManager uses this to set the correct footstep sound variation.

ray.label: Ray Origin
ray.desc: Line trace starts from actor's location (feet level). More reliable than character mesh sockets for surface detection.

trace.label: Trace Direction
trace.desc: Traces straight down by m_TraceDistance units. Configurable in editor - typically 50-100cm to handle stairs and uneven terrain.

physics.label: Physics Query
physics.desc: Critical flag! bReturnPhysicalMaterial must be true or PhysMaterial will always be null. Common gotcha in Unreal audio integration.

channel.label: Visibility Channel
channel.desc: Uses ECC_Visibility channel for traces. Could also use custom trace channel for more precise audio-only collision detection.

mapping.label: Surface Mapping
mapping.desc: Unreal's SurfaceType enums map to Wwise Switch names. Level designers assign Physical Materials to floors, code automatically plays correct footsteps.

creaky.label: Creaky Surfaces
creaky.desc: Special surface types for horror atmosphere. CreakyWood and CreakyStairs have additional random creaking sounds - player reveals position to enemies.

delegate.label: Dynamic Delegate
delegate.desc: DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST allows multiple listeners (audio, UI, gameplay) to subscribe. 'Dynamic' means it works with Blueprints, not just C++.

death.label: Death Sequence
death.desc: Broadcasted when player dies. Triggers death stinger, stops all ambient audio, and starts game over sequence. Critical for audio state management.

blueprint.label: BlueprintAssignable
blueprint.desc: Sound designers can bind Wwise Events directly in Blueprint without touching C++. Iterate on audio faster - no recompile needed.

shutter.label: Camera Shutter
shutter.desc: Core gameplay mechanic - taking photos. Triggers shutter click sound and photo flash audio. Enemy anomalies react to this sound!

zoom.label: Zoom Audio
zoom.desc: Camera zoom triggers servo motor sound and subtle ambience change. Immersive feedback for player entering 'investigation mode'.

photoboard.label: Photoboard UI
photoboard.desc: When viewing collected photos, ambient audio ducks and UI sounds activate. Delegates decouple this from hardcoded audio calls.

config.label: Global Config
config.desc: Audio configuration stored in GameInstance - persists across level loads. Contains Wwise Event references and per-anomaly settings.

retrieval.label: Config Retrieval
retrieval.desc: GetAnomalyAudioConfig returns a Data Asset with all anomaly sound settings. Designers can tweak without recompiling.

binding.label: Event Binding
binding.desc: AddDynamic subscribes to anomaly lifecycle. When anomaly spawns/activates/gets captured, audio responds automatically. Zero coupling with gameplay code.

spatial.label: Spatial Source
spatial.desc: InitializeAudioSource sets up the AkComponent for 3D positioning. Each anomaly has its own audio emitter for proper spatialization.

settings.label: Per-Anomaly Settings
settings.desc: Different anomaly types have unique sounds. GetSettingsForAnomaly looks up the specific audio profile - ghostly whispers vs poltergeist crashes.

switch.label: Wwise Switch
switch.desc: SetSwitch tells Wwise which sound variation to use. One Event, multiple outcomes based on anomaly type. Memory efficient.

post.label: Event Post
post.desc: PostAkEvent triggers the Wwise Event on this specific actor. 3D positioned, respects occlusion/attenuation settings configured in Wwise.

timer.label: Smart Timer
timer.desc: Only starts footstep timer when actually moving. Prevents phantom footsteps when standing still. Timer auto-repeats at configured interval.

cleanup.label: Timer Cleanup
cleanup.desc: Clears timer immediately when movement stops. No lingering footsteps after player halts. Clean state management.

physmat.label: Physical Material
physmat.desc: Critical flag: bReturnPhysicalMaterial must be true. Without it, PhysMaterial is always null - common Unreal audio gotcha.

trace.label: Line Trace
trace.desc: Shoots ray downward to detect floor surface. Uses Visibility channel. Returns surface type for Wwise Switch selection.

hysteresis.label: Hysteresis Gap
hysteresis.desc: Start threshold higher than stop threshold. Enemy at 25% triggers audio, but must drop to 15% to stop. Prevents rapid on/off flickering.

postevent.label: Wwise PostEvent
postevent.desc: UAkGameplayStatics::PostEvent triggers audio on this actor. 3D positioned, respects attenuation curves set in Wwise project.

stopthresh.label: Stop Threshold
stopthresh.desc: Lower threshold for stopping audio. Creates hysteresis band that smooths transitions. No audio stutter when enemy hovers at boundary.

rtpc.label: RTPC Update
rtpc.desc: Real-Time Parameter Control. Sends proximity value to Wwise continuously. Controls volume, filter, pitch - smooth modulation, no steps.

interval.label: Cache Refresh
interval.desc: Only refreshes enemy list every N seconds, not every frame. GetAllActorsOfClass is expensive - caching prevents performance hits.

normalize.label: Normalize Distance
normalize.desc: Converts raw distance to 0-100% range. Inverted: closer enemy = higher value. Audio systems work with normalized values, not world units.

threshold.label: Change Threshold
threshold.desc: Only broadcasts when proximity changes significantly. Prevents audio system spam from micro-movements. Typically 1-5% threshold.

broadcast.label: Event Broadcast
broadcast.desc: Multicast delegate notifies all listeners. Audio manager, UI, gameplay systems all subscribe. Decoupled architecture - no direct dependencies.

sf.concept.title: The Game
sf.concept.subtitle: Black-and-white psychological horror
sf.concept.short: Black-and-white horror game where you photograph paranormal events in a 1960s Irish pub. Sound is your main tool for finding anomalies.
sf.concept.detailed: You have a Polaroid camera and 12 shots. Anomalies happen every 30-50 seconds. Glasses levitate, shadows move on their own, chairs spin. Audio cues tell you where to look: a glass clinks, footsteps echo from nowhere, a chair scrapes across the floor. Without sound, you're blind. Once you capture the evidence, arrange the photos on a corkboard in chronological order to piece together what's happening.
sf.concept.desc:
You're trapped in a black-and-white 1960s Irish pub where reality is breaking down. Anomalies appear every 30 to 50 seconds, and sound is your only tool for finding them. Put on headphones and listen carefully. A glass clinks in the corner. Footsteps echo from an empty hallway. A chair scrapes across the floor by itself. Follow the audio to locate each disturbance, then photograph it. You have exactly 12 shots, so choose wisely.

The pub has constant supernatural activity. Glasses levitate off the bar. Shadows detach from their owners and move independently. Chairs spin on their own. The grainy black-and-white aesthetic makes everything feel like a forgotten photograph from decades ago.

Audio is the core mechanic. Mute the game and you can't find anomalies. You won't know where to look, what's happening, or how to survive. Every creak, whisper, and crash is information.

Once you've captured your evidence, race to the corkboard and arrange the photos in the correct chronological order. This is how you piece together what's happening and why. But work quickly. Something is hunting you through the pub, and time is running out.
sf.gameplay.title: Core Mechanic: Observe → Capture → Connect
sf.gameplay.observe_desc: Anomalies appear every 30-50 seconds. Environmental sounds guide you to their location.
sf.gameplay.capture_desc: Use your Polaroid camera to photograph the anomaly. You have limited film, and every reload leaves you vulnerable.
sf.gameplay.connect_desc: Arrange photos on the pin board in the correct order to reveal the truth and reach the good ending.
sf.audio_systems.title: Audio Implementation
sf.audio_systems.rtpc_desc: Ambient sound and player breathing get more intense with each anomaly that spawns. More anomalies = higher tension.
sf.audio_systems.switches_desc: Each room has its own ambient layers that crossfade as you move. Bathroom has spatialized toilet and faucet sounds. Footsteps change based on surface. Wood, tiles, concrete.
sf.audio_systems.delegates_desc: Audio systems communicate through delegates. C++ handles game logic, Blueprint handles audio. Keeps everything modular. Change one without breaking the other.
sf.audio_systems.spatial_desc: Full 3D positional audio for anomalies, enemy, and environmental cues. Spatial accuracy is required for gameplay. You can't find threats without it.
sf.dev_tools.title: Development Tools
sf.dev_tools.fixer_desc: Custom C++ plugin that restores Wwise integration after Perforce pulls. Runs automatically, no manual fixing needed.
sf.dev_tools.rebuilder_desc: Deletes Intermediate and Saved folders, regenerates project files. Fixes linker errors that happen after bad merges. Takes 2 minutes instead of hunting through folders manually.

sf.anomalies.title: Anomaly Types
sf.anomalies.desc: Semi-randomized disturbances that escalate as the game progresses.
sf.anomalies.object_desc: Chairs rotate on their own, glasses levitate mid-air, and cutlery clatters without cause. Everyday objects begin to defy the laws of physics.
sf.anomalies.env_desc: The space itself warps and distorts. Radio static erupts from nowhere, lights flicker erratically, and the clock accelerates its ticking.
sf.anomalies.shadow_desc: Human silhouettes materialize in the darkness. Shadows peel away from their source objects and move independently. Motion occurs in places where no light source could cast it.

sf.footstep.title: Footstep System: Surface Detection & Audio Routing
sf.footstep.desc: Footsteps change based on what you're walking on. Wood, tiles, concrete. The system detects the surface and switches sounds in Wwise automatically.
sf.footstep.what: C++ component does a line trace down from the player, checks the Physical Material, and maps it to a Wwise Switch (Tiles, Wood, CreakyWood, Concrete).
sf.footstep.how: Physical Material is detected using Unreal's surface system. That gets mapped to a Switch name. Blueprint Audio Manager gets the delegate and plays the right sound in Wwise.
sf.footstep.why: C++ handles detection, Blueprint handles audio. I can add new surfaces without touching C++ code. Audio designer can change Switch names in Wwise without code changes.
sf.footstep.result: Footsteps match every surface automatically. No manual work needed. Adding new materials is straightforward.
sf.player_audio.title: Player Audio System: Delegate-Based Communication
sf.player_audio.desc: Player actions trigger audio through delegates. Camera shot, zoom, photoboard interaction. Each action calls the right Wwise event.
sf.player_audio.what: PlayerCharacter (C++) defines multicast delegates. When you take a photo or zoom, the delegate broadcasts. Blueprint Audio Manager listens and plays the sound.
sf.player_audio.how: DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE creates delegates that work with Blueprint. UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable) allows binding in Blueprint. Multicast means multiple listeners can react to one action.
sf.player_audio.why: PlayerCharacter doesn't know anything about audio. Audio Manager doesn't know anything about player logic. I can test and change each independently.
sf.player_audio.result: Adding new audio actions is easy. No hardcoded calls. Audio designers can change sounds in Wwise without touching player code.
sf.rtpc.title: Dynamic Tension System: RTPC-Driven Ambience
sf.rtpc.desc: More photos on the board = higher tension. Ambient intensity increases as you progress.
sf.rtpc.what: RTPC value (0-5) controls ambient layers in Wwise. PhotoboardWidget tracks how many photos you've placed. More photos = higher RTPC value = more intense ambience.
sf.rtpc.how: When you place a photo, UpdateAmbientRTPC() finds the AkAmbientSound actor (tagged 'AmbientProgressive') and sets the RTPC value. Wwise crossfades between ambient layers based on that value.
sf.rtpc.why: RTPC gives smooth transitions between tension states. No audio jumps. I control crossfade curves in Wwise without touching code.
sf.rtpc.result: Tension builds smoothly as you progress. Tweak curves in Wwise, atmosphere adapts automatically.
sf.wwise_arch.title: Wwise Architecture: Switch Containers & Photoboard Integration
sf.wwise_arch.desc: Switch Containers work with the RTPC system. More photos collected = different ambient layers activate.
sf.wwise_arch.what: RTPC value (0-5 from photos) drives Switch Container selection in Wwise. Each Switch state has different ambient layers. RTPC handles smooth crossfades, Switch Containers handle structural changes.
sf.wwise_arch.how: PhotoboardWidget sends RTPC value. Wwise uses that to pick the right Switch state and crossfade between layers.
sf.wwise_arch.why: Switch Containers give discrete layer control. RTPC gives smooth transitions. Together: structural changes (different ambient sets) and intensity progression.
sf.wwise_arch.result: Ambient responds to player progress. This is partial implementation. Full system will have more layers and complexity.

sf.anomaly_audio.title: 3-Stage Anomaly Detection
sf.anomaly_audio.description: Every anomaly triggers three audio layers:
sf.anomaly_audio.alert: Alert (0.5s): Static burst marks the spawn
sf.anomaly_audio.hint: Hint (1-2s): Directional sound points you there
sf.anomaly_audio.conclusion: No visuals, no UI markers, just sound. Audio is the detection system.
sf.challenges.title: Challenges & Solutions
sf.challenges.desc: Problems encountered during development and how I addressed them.
sf.challenges.challenge1.title: Workflow Optimization Tools
sf.challenges.challenge1.problem: Multi-institutional student project had workflow problems. Wwise integration broke after Perforce pulls. Unreal compilation took too long, causing downtime.
sf.challenges.challenge1.solution: Built Wwise Unreal Fixer and Unreal Engine Rebuilder. Wwise Fixer restores broken integration after Perforce pulls (one click). Rebuilder automates compilation to cut downtime. Made these to help the student team work faster.
sf.code_explanations.footstep_what: Function detects surface type under player using line trace downward from player position.
sf.code_explanations.footstep_how: Validates owner and world exist, then performs line trace using ECC_WorldStatic channel. Checks object's Physical Material and maps SurfaceType enum to Wwise Switch name (Tiles, Wood, CreakyWood, Concrete).
sf.code_explanations.footstep_why: Using Physical Material allows automatic detection without manually tagging each surface. The enum-to-Switch mapping is a one-time setup that connects Unreal's surface system to Wwise - this is configuration, not hardcoded audio calls. Audio designer can modify Switch names in Wwise without code changes.
sf.code_explanations.delegate_what: Definition of multicast delegates for player actions that trigger audio events.
sf.code_explanations.delegate_how: DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE creates delegate that can be broadcast from C++ and listened to in Blueprint. UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable) allows binding in Blueprint.
sf.code_explanations.delegate_why: Multicast delegates allow multiple listeners (e.g. Audio Manager) to react to one action. Dynamic delegates work with Blueprint, giving audio designer full control without modifying C++ code.
sf.code_explanations.rtpc_what: Function updates RTPC value in Wwise based on number of photos placed on board.
sf.code_explanations.rtpc_how: Validates world exists, then finds AkAmbientSound actor by tag 'AmbientProgressive' (more efficient and reliable than name string search). Sets RTPC value (0-5) corresponding to number of important photos. Wwise automatically crossfades between ambient layers.
sf.code_explanations.rtpc_why: RTPC = smooth transitions. I tweak crossfade curves in Wwise, no code changes needed.
sf.enemy_presence.title: Enemy Presence Audio System
sf.enemy_presence.desc: Audio gets more intense as enemy gets closer. Two layers: ambient dread + character breathing.
sf.enemy_presence.what: System tracks enemy distance and triggers audio layers. Closer enemy = more intense audio. Dread ambience and breathing stress scale with proximity.
sf.enemy_presence.how: OnProximityChanged() receives proximity value (0-100%), starts/stops dread layers, updates RTPC for intensity, adjusts breathing stress. All validated with null safety checks.
sf.enemy_presence.why: RTPC = no hard audio cuts when enemy moves. Breathing layer adds urgency without cluttering the mix.
sf.enemy_presence.result: Closer enemy = louder dread + faster breathing. Smooth transitions, no audio pops.
sf.ambience_zones.title: Ambience Zone System
sf.ambience_zones.desc: Location-based audio that changes as you move through different areas of the pub.
sf.ambience_zones.what: 5 distinct zones with unique ambient soundscapes: Main Bar, Back Room, Bathroom, Hallway, Storage. Each has specific audio atmosphere.
sf.ambience_zones.how: Trigger volumes detect player location. On zone enter, fade out previous ambience and fade in new zone's layers. Smooth crossfades prevent audio jumps.
sf.ambience_zones.why: Each room has distinct acoustics. Bathroom: tiles + reverb. Bar: glasses + crowd murmur. Helps player orient by sound.
sf.ambience_zones.result: Walk from bar to bathroom, audio crossfades in 500ms. No pops, no silence gaps.
sf.anomaly_system.title: Anomaly Audio System
sf.anomaly_system.desc: 3-stage detection system for 10 different paranormal anomaly types with unique audio signatures.
sf.anomaly_system.what: 3 detection stages: Far (general alert), Medium (directional cue), Close (precise location). 10 anomaly types including Levitating Glass, Shadow Movement, Spinning Chair.
sf.anomaly_system.how: Distance-based RTPC drives audio intensity. Directional audio guides player to anomaly. Each anomaly type has unique sound signature for identification.
sf.anomaly_system.why: Sound is the primary detection mechanic. Alert signals spawn, hint gives direction, presence loop confirms location.
sf.anomaly_system.result: Playtesters find anomalies by ear. 80% detection rate after adding directional hints.

project_amorak_block1_content: The creature needed to sound massive. I layered 4 animal recordings: lion, elephant, tiger, and hippo. Pitching them down created weight, while the hippo texture added a unique high-end rasp. Using real animals made it feel alive rather than synthetic.
project_amorak_block2_content: I designed the environment to follow the camera. Dripping water is close and unsettling, while distant chains suggest a larger threat. Binaural panning places every sound in a specific spot around the listener's head.
project_amorak_block3_content: The mix prioritizes the creature. I used dynamic ducking to push the environment down whenever the monster screams or the character breathes, ensuring the most important narrative elements are always clear.
project_nottoday_block1_content: Side-scrolling 1-4 player racing game. It's chaotic, loud, and ridiculous. Audio Designer & Technical Implementer. I did everything audio: recording, sound design, music choice, and implementation.
project_nottoday_block2_content: I didn't want the engines to sound like looped MP3s. I built a graph in MetaSounds where the kart's pitch and rattle intensity change based on speed. You can hear the difference when you drive from carpet to tiles—the sound reacts instantly.
sf.block.enemy_desc: Dynamic audio system that responds to enemy proximity. Creates tension through dread layers and stressed breathing. System tracks enemy distance and triggers audio layers. Closer enemy = more intense audio.
sf.block.mixer_desc: Switch Containers work with the RTPC system. More photos collected = different ambient layers activate. RTPC value (0-5 from photos) drives Switch Container selection in Wwise.
sf.block.anomaly_desc: 3-stage detection system for 10 different paranormal anomaly types with unique audio signatures. Distance-based RTPC drives audio intensity. Directional audio guides player to anomaly.
sf.block.dialogue_desc: Clean separation between player actions and audio responses using Blueprint delegates. System connects player actions (camera shot, zoom) with appropriate Wwise events.
